teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji beat Japan 34-28 as Ben Volavola's penalties seal win
teams.body: Jake White's first Test in charge ended in a 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo on Saturday. The win reversed September's Pacific Nations Cup final, lost 20-15 to Japan. Both teams scored three first-half tries, and substitute Ben Volavola settled it with two penalties after the break. White picked no Europe-based players and handed out four new caps, and he says Fiji "can beat anyone" on their day.

lead.why: Fiji's first Test under Jake White produced a new result, and it is the team's own news ahead of the European tour.

teams.heading: Borthwick could call George Barton and Nathan Jibulu into November squad
teams.body: Planet Rugby has named seven uncapped players Steve Borthwick could draft into England's November Tests, and Gloucester full-back George Barton heads the case, its writer arguing his form has pushed him into the picture. Sale hooker Nathan Jibulu is another name to watch: two man-of-the-match displays this season, and Jamie George is nearing the end of his Test career. England's block also features Australia, Japan and the All Blacks.

lead.why: It is the only shortlisted England men's Test story not already run, and it concerns national squad selection for November.

teams.heading: Billy Searle turns down France return to stay at Leicester Tigers
teams.body: Leicester fly-half Billy Searle turned down a potential return to France to stay at Welford Road, telling BBC Radio Leicester he wanted to "push his game on" in England. The 30-year-old signed a three-year extension in September, having already had three spells in French rugby, at Toulouse, Biarritz and Agen. "I had interest in France but I made it clear I wanted to stay," he said. He also hasn't given up on a first senior England cap.

lead.why: Alldritt and the Menier tributes have already run, and this is the freshest France-linked item left, with a player who could have returned to France choosing England's Tigers instead.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell names 36-man Ireland squad for November Test window
teams.body: Andy Farrell has named a 36-man squad for Ireland's November Test window, with Argentina the next opponent, and The42 Rugby Weekly has been picking over the selections. The same week carries a big interpro, with a blockbuster Leinster-Munster URC clash in Dublin. Planet Rugby's Ulster ratings, meanwhile, called Stuart McCloskey's display a 'statement performance' that puts Farrell on notice just before the Nations Championship.

lead.why: Farrell's 36-man November squad is a fresh Test-level selection item, and the other fresh candidates are club ratings or a women's match.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 at home to South Africa in November 2025
teams.body: Italy lost 32-14 at home to South Africa in November 2025, in an International Friendly. That is a single result, not a head-to-head record, so it does not establish a wider pattern between the sides. Italy's own run is the more pressing number: across the last three games in the log they have lost every one, conceding 131 points. The next meeting is Round 4 of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Former Scotland winger Tim Visser to go on trial charged with rape
teams.body: Tim Visser, capped 33 times by Scotland as a winger between 2012 and 2017, is to go on trial accused of controlling, abusing and raping a woman. The 39-year-old faces four charges spanning 14 years, from 2010 to 2024, two of which allege rape, including sex after consent was withdrawn. He has entered a not-guilty plea at a hearing in the High Court in Glasgow, and the trial is set for January 2028 in Edinburgh.

lead.why: It is the most widely covered item not already run on this tab, and it concerns a former Scotland capped player.

teams.heading: Taulupe Faletau needs finger surgery, Wales hope he's back for November
teams.body: Faletau's comeback has come undone. The Cardiff number eight, 35 and on 109 Wales caps, will have surgery on a finger injured in his first game since March, and he misses the URC derby at Ospreys. Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "He will miss the Ospreys game but hopefully after November he will be fine." Steve Tandy left him out of the Nations Championship squad and has said he needs to show durability before any return.

lead.why: A fresh injury to a Wales great with a November Nations Championship question attached, and it is not one of the stories already run this week.

teams.heading: Les Kiss names 33-man spring squad with Tom Lambert among new faces
teams.body: Les Kiss has named a 33-man squad for the spring tour, and the new faces are the story. Prop Tom Lambert is in as a newcomer alongside Teddy Wilson, while centre Len Ikitau is back from injury. Tupou and Hooper return too, after Australia were without them against New Zealand because those Tests fell outside the global player release window. Ryan Lonergan is the standout No. 9, with Wilson and Tate McDermott pushing for the back-up spot.

lead.why: Items 1 and 2 have already run, so the full 33-man squad, with its new faces and returns, is the strongest remaining Test-squad story.

teams.heading: Dentsu returns to acquire Rugby World Cup 2027 rights in Japan
teams.body: Dentsu is returning to acquire the rights to Rugby World Cup 2027 in Japan, a bid that determines how the men's tournament is shown to Japanese fans. The bid itself is the news; the terms and any rivals remain unclear. Meanwhile the team is on the back foot, sitting 10 of 12 on the log after losing to Fiji, with the next Test a trip to Wales in Round four.

lead.why: The only shortlisted item that is new and about Japan's own rugby interests; the Kolbe piece is a club reminiscence and the Wales items are women's WXV coverage.

teams.heading: Captain Ardie Savea among All Blacks unavailable for Europe tour
teams.body: Captain Ardie Savea is among the All Blacks unavailable for the Europe tour, with a shoulder injury adding to a growing list. Wing Leroy Carter was ruled out after ankle surgery following a hip-drop tackle in the first Bledisloe Cup Test in Auckland, and Ruben Love, Luke Jacobson, Caleb Clarke, Billy Proctor, Ollie Norris and Tamaiti Williams are also unavailable. The tour takes in Scotland, England and Wales before the Twickenham finals weekend.

lead.why: It is the only NEW men's Test-squad item on the shortlist, and it names the captain among the unavailable players.
